scope: bounded primary-source comparison of all-p weak regularity for finite-dimensional KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups
status: literature-interface-only; no proof or priority claim

opportunities.proposed_statement: For every finite-dimensional faithful-state KMS-symmetric QMS generator L and every positive definite observable f, establish E_p(f) >= E_2(I_{2,p}(f)) for all 1 <= p <= 2. By KMS p-q duality, this would imply E_p(f) >= (1/(p-1)) E_2(I_{2,p}(f)) for p >= 2.
opportunities.quantifiers_and_domain: Finite-dimensional matrix algebra; faithful stationary state sigma; Heisenberg generator self-adjoint in the KMS weighted pairing. Positive definite f is the safe source domain, especially at p=1 where the logarithmic formula is displayed. The derivation of the high-p branch uses positive f and the power-map composition law.
opportunities.historical_importance: The low-p interval is the missing pointwise Dirichlet-form interface between an endpoint entropy-production estimate and full weak Lp regularity. It is stronger than a p=1 endpoint statement and distinct from an MLSI comparison.
strongest_checked_prior: Kastoryano-Temme, arXiv:1207.3261v2, Definition 9, Eqs. (31)-(32): weak regularity is conjectured in Conjecture 19; the printed high-p weak coefficient is p-1 and is inconsistent with their strong coefficient and a positive-input tracial qubit perturbation.
Beigi-Datta-Rouze, arXiv:1804.10100v2, Theorem 14 and Proposition 8: Stroock-Varopoulos and p-q duality under strong sigma-reversibility, i.e. GNS symmetry, not arbitrary KMS symmetry.
Bardet, arXiv:1710.01039v1, Theorem 4.1: strong 2/p profile under sigma_Tr-DBC; Eq. (4.3) repeats the p-1 high-p weak coefficient.
Gao-Wang, arXiv:2609.20753v2, Section 3.1 and Theorem B: an MLSI comparison route that avoids assuming strong Lp regularity, but no pointwise weak-Lp theorem.
opportunities.concrete_transfer: For p >= 2 set r=p/(p-1), g=I_{r,p}(f). The source power maps give I_{p,r}(g)=f and I_{2,r}(g)=I_{2,p}(f); KMS self-adjointness gives E_r(g)=(p-1)E_p(f). Thus the low branch implies exactly the reciprocal coefficient 1/(p-1). This is an algebraic transfer, not a result filling 1<p<2.
opportunities.load_bearing_missing_lemma: A proof or counterexample for the positive-input low-p inequality at some/all 1<p<2 under KMS symmetry alone. No checked endpoint-to-interval interpolation theorem supplies it.
compatibility_obligations: Keep the Heisenberg generator and KMS weighted pairing conventions fixed.
Do not replace KMS symmetry by the stronger GNS/detailed-balance hypothesis used by the Stroock-Varopoulos theorems.
Keep positive-input/logarithmic p=1 domains explicit; do not infer an unspecified extension to sign-indefinite Hermitians.
Treat the printed p-1 high-p coefficient as a source inconsistency; do not silently amend it or attribute the reciprocal formula to the authors.
opportunities.early_falsification_test: Use the primitive tracial qubit depolarizer and positive perturbations f=I+epsilon Z to test any proposed universal coefficient at each p; the ratio E_p(f)/E_2(I_{2,p}f) tends to 2/p. In particular this falsifies the literal printed p-1 high-p inequality for p>2, while it does not falsify the reciprocal weak profile.
opportunities.significance_if_established: Would settle the all-p weak profile from a single low-p estimate and provide a genuine KMS-symmetric counterpart to the GNS Stroock-Varopoulos transfer. It would not by itself prove strong regularity or any complete/reference-amplified version.
opportunities.status_of_arbitrary_KMS_low_interval: UNKNOWN in this bounded primary-source audit; no checked theorem or matched counterexample.

source_formula_warning: The reciprocal high-p coefficient is derived from KMS p-q duality. The checked KT arXiv v2 and journal versions and Bardet Eq. (4.3) literally print p-1; preserve that fact. No erratum was located in the bounded search, which is not evidence that none exists.
